title: Targeted Proteomic LC-MS/MS Analysis
author: Yan Chen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf9xjr7n
materials: Thaw peptide samples On ice , and transfer 30 µL of each sample to LC autosampler vials (Agilent, Cat.# 5182-0567, 5182-0564) or 96-well plate (Bio-Rad, Cat.# HSP9655).

Samples were loaded on the temperature controlled autosampler at 4 °C . The Agilent 1290 Infinity II UHPLC is equipped with a Sigma–Aldrich Ascentis Peptides ES-C18 analytical column ( 2.1 mm, ID , 50 mm, length , 2.7 µm, particle size , and 160-Å pore size (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat.# 53301-U)) coupled to a 2.1 mm, ID , 5 mm, length guard column (Sigma-Aldrich, Cat.# 53536-U) with the same particle and pore size. The column is operated at 60 °C .

steps.title: Perform Instrument Maintenance and Calibration
steps.instruction: Ensure the Agilent 6460 QQQ mass spectrometer and 1290 Infinity II UHPLC system are calibrated and performing optimally.

substeps.instruction: Perform a full autotune of the mass spectrometer at least quarterly (or more frequently if necessary) using Agilent Tune Mix (Catalog #G1969-85000) to optimize ion transmission and update EM voltage.
Perform a check tune prior to analyzing a batch of samples to verify resolution and mass accuracy.
Track UHPLC-QQQ performance daily by injecting 50 fmol BSA tryptic digest standard and monitoring eight BSA peptides via a scheduled MRM assay for retention time, peak shape, and peak intensity.
Automate performance tracking via the PanoramaWeb server using the AutoQC pipeline.

steps.title: Prepare LC-MS/MS Separation
steps.instruction: Separate peptides using the Agilent 1290 Infinity II UHPLC system coupled to an Agilent 6460 QQQ mass spectrometer.

substeps.instruction: Load 20 µg of peptides from each sample onto the column.
Set the flow rate to 0.4 ml/min.
Apply a linear mobile-phase gradient over 10 minutes using Solvent A (0.1% formic acid in water) and Solvent B (0.1% formic acid in acetonitrile).

steps.title: Configure Ionization and Data Acquisition
steps.instruction: Ionize eluted peptides and acquire raw mass spectrometry data.

substeps.instruction: Use an Agilent Jet Stream ESI source operating in positive ion mode.
Acquire MS raw data using Agilent MassHunter version B.08.02 (or B.06.01).

Monitor SRM transitions using scanning or scheduled MRM mode with the following criteria: minimum dwell time of 2 ms per transition, maximum of 200 concurrent transitions, and a total cycle time of less than 1.5 sec.

steps.title: Analyze and Validate SRM Data
steps.instruction: Process the acquired SRM data using Skyline software version 20.1.

substeps.instruction: Import acquired SRM data into Skyline.
For small sample sets: Visually check and validate peak integration by browsing replicate peak area and retention time tabs.
For large sample sets (>100 samples): Complete peak integration using Skyline advanced peak picking models, such as mProphet.

steps.title: Export and Archive Results
steps.instruction: Export the quantitative data and archive the method information.

substeps.instruction: Export the peptide quantitative report to a .csv file.
Upload the Skyline file containing the data and SRM methods information to a project folder on the PanoramaWeb server.
